name: Fufu with Light Soup
summary: A thin, fiery tomato and ginger broth with chicken, served with stretchy cassava and plantain fufu.
story: Light soup, or nkwan, is a thin, peppery Ghanaian broth eaten with fufu pounded from cassava and plantain. It is a classic Sunday and celebration meal, and also comforting when someone has a cold.

items.name: dried herbs (curry leaf or basil)
items.note: or a few fresh basil leaves

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Blend half the onion with the ginger, garlic and one scotch bonnet. Rub this over the chicken with some salt and leave it to marinate for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Start the broth
steps.text: Put the chicken in a pot with the water, sliced onion and stock cube. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then simmer for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Add the tomato
steps.text: Blend the tomatoes with the remaining scotch bonnet and add to the pot with the garden eggs. Simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes until the chicken is falling tender and the broth is deep red-orange.

steps.title: Finish the soup
steps.text: Mash the garden eggs into the soup for body and add the herbs. Taste for salt and pepper; it should taste hot, gingery and savoury. Keep warm.

steps.title: Boil the fufu base
steps.text: Boil the cassava and plantain in water for 20-25 minutes until a fork slides in with no resistance. Drain, keeping a cup of the water.

steps.title: Pound the fufu
steps.text: Pound in a large mortar, adding a little water, until smooth, sticky and stretchy with no lumps. Alternatively, mash then process in a food processor in short bursts, scraping often.

steps.title: Shape and serve
steps.text: Wet your hands and shape the fufu into smooth balls. Place in bowls, ladle soup and chicken around it and eat by pinching off pieces and swallowing without chewing.

tips: Do not skimp on ginger and pepper; the soup is meant to be sharp and clear.
Overboiled tomatoes make the broth cloudy, so simmer gently.
Fufu must be pounded hot; cold cassava will not become smooth.
Fish or goat can replace chicken; adjust time accordingly.

swaps.swap: Instant fufu flour from African shops, or yam and plantain mash; texture is slightly softer.
Small green aubergine or Thai aubergine gives similar bitterness.
